lines.text: Most adults can take Fybogel, including while pregnant or breastfeeding.
Only give Fybogel to a child under 6 years old if it's been prescribed by a doctor.

cards.headline: Who may not be able to take Fybogel

lines.text: Fybogel is not suitable for some people. To make sure it's safe for you, tell your doctor or pharmacist before taking Fybogel if you have:
ever had an allergic reaction to Fybogel or any other medicine
any changes in your poo, such as having blood in it, or how often you need to poo, which are unusual for you and has lasted longer than 2 weeks
tummy pain and you feel sick or are being sick, these could be signs of a blockage in your bowel
muscle weakness of the bowel (colonic atony)
difficulty swallowing or any throat problems
a rare genetic condition called phenylketonuria

cards.headline: Dosage and how to take Fybogel

lines.text: Dosage
The usual dose of Fybogel for constipation is:
for adults and children aged 12 years and over – 1 sachet of granules twice a day
for children aged 6 to 11 years – half to 1 level (5ml) teaspoonful of granules twice a day
for children aged 5 years or under – half to 1 level (5ml) teaspoonful of granules twice a day, only if recommended by a doctor
It's best to take Fybogel after a meal or snack and at least 30 minutes before or after you take any other medicine.
To make up the medicine, open the sachet and empty the amount of granules you need into a glass. Add at least 150ml of cold water to the glass.
Stir well until all the granules have dissolved and the Fybogel solution is clear or slightly hazy, then drink it immediately.
Try not to breathe in the powder when you make up the Fybogel drink, because there's a small chance this could trigger a mild allergic reaction.
Have your evening drink of Fybogel at least an hour before going to bed. Do not drink Fybogel just before you go to sleep because this can make it harder for your bowel to move the poo along.

It's important to drink extra fluid if you're taking Fybogel. Adults should try to drink more than 2 litres, or around 8 glasses, of fluid each day. If you do not drink enough fluid while taking Fybogel, your constipation may get worse.
Fybogel is commonly taken during pregnancy and is not harmful to your baby.
You can take Fybogel while breastfeeding.
It does not pass into breast milk so has not caused any side effects in breastfed babies.
It’s important to drink plenty of fluids while taking Fybogel, and this will also help with your breast milk supply.
Fybogel can change the way some medicines work.
Tell your pharmacist or doctor if you're taking any other medicines before you start to take Fybogel, including:
lithium, a medicine for mood problems
carbamazepine, a medicine for epilepsy and mood problems
digoxin, a heart medicine
insulin or any other medicine for diabetes
mesalazine, a medicine to treat bowel disease
pain medicines that can cause constipation, such as codeine
These are not all the medicines that may cause problems if you take them with Fybogel. For a full list, see the leaflet inside your medicine packet.

Fybogel can affect how other medicines, vitamins and supplements are absorbed in your body. If you need to take another medicine or a supplement, take it more than an hour before or after you take Fybogel.
Sometimes you may need to take 2 different types of laxatives at the same time to get your bowel moving.
Only take 2 types of laxatives together if a doctor or pharmacist has recommended it because it can increase your chance of side effects.
You can take Fybogel at the same time as IBS remedies such as Buscopan.
